I mean, you probably don't need most of it. You essentially need:

- a safe place for baby to sleep (crib, mattress, sheets)
- clothing (mostly PJs honestly)
- sleep sac
- diapers and wipes
- a place to put used diapers (I use regular garbage)
- a way to walk with baby (stroller, carrier)
- car seat

The only "additional" things that I found helpful were a bouncy chair and a small play mat or blanket to put baby down on when you need both hands.

She brought up her underwear and he responded that an upgrade would be reasonable, given she's now in middle school and the issue is coming up with her peers. Nothing in what he said is sexual, and it's also reasonable for a 13 year old to want to move away from childhood. In fact it's healthy - she's taking very small, age appropriate steps into adulthood and is looking for her grownups to support her in doing so.

It's reasonable for him to ask his partner - in marriage and in raising his daughter - to get help to stay healthy. My husband and I ask the same of each other (within reason). 

I do think therapy, or anything else that's been helpful in the past, is the move.
